editorial.headline: Private Primary Education, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This private primary-education activity spans general learning for children aged seven to twelve, with a fully open national foreign-ownership ceiling and no Bali PMA moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
This activity concerns privately provided primary education for pupils aged seven to twelve, along with related equivalency education. Its centre of gravity is general knowledge and practical skills: the foundational work associated with private primary schools, private primary special-education schools, and private Paket A provision. The scope also includes formal primary-level education delivered through cooperation between a foreign educational institution accredited or recognised in its home country and an Indonesian educational institution, within the applicable legal framework.

It is a broad private-education category in terms of business scale. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar enterprises, placing small providers and larger educational operators within the same activity classification. That breadth matters because the subject is not a narrow specialist service; it is the private delivery and management of general primary education, including forms designed for learners requiring special education and recognised equivalency routes.

Nationally, the activity is marked TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. In plain terms, the record does not place a national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. That is a material point for founders assessing whether a foreign-owned education operator can sit within the national investment framework, rather than assuming that primary education is closed merely because it is socially consequential.

Bali requires its own reading. The provincial moratorium permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island. Yet this activity is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and is not marked as blocked: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which places it outside that moratorium block. Nationally open does not erase Bali’s screen, but here the record says that screen does not block PMA registration. On the record’s terms, a foreign-owned operator is therefore not barred from registering this activity in Bali today.
